phase-428 W5 (2026-09-06) ledgered a recorded sweep finding, RANKED-9, the whole class in one row: seven call sites across five verbs (`create_service` and `create_client` each appear twice).

UPSTREAM'S CONTRACT: `rclcpp::Node::create_*` either returns a usable entity or THROWS. A non-null return is a promise.

OURS NOW (`packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/rclcpp.hpp`, the `rclcpp::Node` adapter), re-measured 2026-09-23: every factory passes the inner `nros::Result` to `detail::require_created` (`:328`) — `create_publisher` at `:519`, `create_subscription` `:584`, `create_wall_timer` `:637`, `create_service` `:686` / `:702`, `create_client` `:727` / `:743` — which on failure calls `abort_failed_create` (`:320`): `NROS_ERROR` naming the verb, the entity name and the `nros::ErrorCode`, then the `NROS_RCLCPP_ABORT_FAILED_CREATE` text (`rclcpp/logging.hpp:203`) naming the underlying `nros::Node` verbs that return the `Result` for a caller who wants to handle it, then `std::abort()`. `require_created` takes the `Result` BY VALUE so the `[[nodiscard]]` is consumed there and cannot be dropped a second time. A returned pointer is therefore an initialised entity, which is upstream's promise minus the throw.

HOW A USER FINDS OUT: the process dies at the failing create naming it. The remaining silence is one frame UP — constructing a `Node` before `rclcpp::init()` yields `initialized() == false` with no diagnostic until the first create (`cpp:Node::Node`), and `rclcpp::spin` / `spin_some` (`:894` / `:901`) still return without a word on such a node; with every create aborting, that path is only reachable by a node that created nothing.

WHY `divergence` AND NOT `gap`. The difference is "upstream throws, we terminate", and no exceptions is one of the constraints SCHEMA.md names as sanctioning a divergence. RFC-0018 states it twice — "No exceptions: compile with `-fno-exceptions`" and the Key Differences row "Exceptions for errors -> `Result` return values / No exceptions on embedded" — and `rclcpp/rclcpp.hpp:290-320` weighs each alternative (a `Result`-returning overload, a null `shared_ptr`, an `ok()` flag) and concludes that aborting at the create is the loudest answer available. That is a decision, not a hole. The 2026-09-21 statement held the verdict at `gap` on the ground that "a hosted build with exceptions could throw `rclcpp::exceptions::RCLError` here instead of aborting, and nobody has done it". MEASURED 2026-09-23: `NROS_CPP_EXCEPTIONS`, RFC-0018's own name for that mode ("strictly opt-in and never the default"), occurs NOWHERE under `packages/`, `cmake/` or `examples/` — the mode does not exist, so there is no build in which the throw would be reachable. If one is ever built, this is the row to re-open.

Disposition ADOPT: the information exists at the create, so the refusal fires at the earliest point the defect is KNOWABLE, and nothing in RFC-0018 requires a non-null pointer to a dead entity.

The counts are unchanged: seven sites, five verbs.

History, one sentence: until phase-428 Q1 (2026-09-06) each of the seven sites discarded the `Result` with an explicit `(void)` and returned a non-null pointer to an entity whose `initialized_` was false, so a ported node built clean, published into nothing and `spin` returned immediately with exit code 0 — SILENTLY WRONG, the exact shape RFC-0089's "return type, where the result is discarded" row calls non-mechanical. So `node->create_publisher<M>("chatter", 10)` compiles on a freestanding target, which it did not before; `ported_create_publisher_freestanding_probe.cpp` INVERTED from an expected-failure to a positive compile in the same commit.

The `require_created` contract this row records is unchanged, and so is the failure channel and the count: still seven sites across five verbs, because the two `std::string` `create_publisher` overloads forward to the one `const char*` body rather than each calling `require_created`.

One behaviour DID change and it is stated rather than left to be found: the node no longer co-owns the publisher. `Owned<T>` is sole ownership, so the `hosted().owned_entities` push is gone — the entity dies with the holder, which for the ported member pattern is when the node dies, i.e. what upstream does when the node was the last owner. What no longer happens is a publisher outliving its own handle. See `cpp:Owned` and `cpp:Publisher::make_shared`.
